reference.title: Performance vs scalability
reference.lede: A service is scalable if adding resources results in a proportional increase in performance.

reference.title: Latency vs throughput
reference.lede: Latency is the time to perform an action. Throughput is the number of actions per unit of time.

reference.title: CAP theorem
reference.lede: Pick two. Networks fail, so partition tolerance isn't the one you drop.

reference.title: Consistency patterns
reference.lede: With multiple copies of the same data, decide how they agree — and how long agreement takes.

reference.title: Availability patterns
reference.lede: Two complementary patterns support high availability: fail-over and replication.

reference.title: Domain name system
reference.lede: Translates a domain name to an IP address — a hierarchical, heavily cached lookup before any request is made.

reference.title: Content delivery network
reference.lede: A globally distributed network of proxy servers, serving content from locations closer to the user.

reference.title: Load balancer
reference.lede: Distribute requests across resources so no single one is a bottleneck or a single point of failure.

reference.title: Reverse proxy
reference.lede: A single web server front that makes internal services look like one origin.

reference.title: Application layer
reference.lede: Separate the web layer from the application layer so each scales — and fails — independently.

reference.title: Asynchronism
reference.lede: Move expensive work out of the request path.

reference.title: Communication
reference.lede: TCP, UDP, RPC and REST — four different bargains between guarantees and speed.

reference.title: Cache
reference.lede: Absorb hot reads close to the caller. Pay in staleness and invalidation.

reference.title: Scaling a relational database
reference.lede: Five levers, five different bills.

reference.title: NoSQL
reference.lede: A collection of data items represented in a key-value store, document store, wide column store, or graph database.

reference.title: SQL or NoSQL
reference.lede: Structured data with transactions, or unstructured data at scale. Pick on the shape of the reads.

reference.title: How to approach the question
reference.lede: Four steps: outline the use cases, sketch a high level design, design core components, then scale it.

reference.title: Back-of-the-envelope estimation
reference.lede: Powers of two, latency numbers, and a willingness to round hard.

reference.title: Latency numbers
reference.lede: Each step is roughly ten times the last. This is why memory beats disk and why the round trip is the enemy.

reference.title: Security
reference.lede: Encrypt in transit and at rest, sanitize input, and grant the least privilege that works.
